meta.sub: Scored from source: a shallow clone of github.com/treeverse/lakeFS at 4bb11638 (2026-08-16), read by a 14-agent pass — 5 subsystem recon readers, 4 dimension scorers, 4 adversarial verifiers demanding file:line evidence, 1 comparison critic. Reconciliation: misconfig lowered by a verifier, CAS raised and upgrades trimmed by the critic, failure shape lowered 4→3 in post-publication review. One column, two postures — server API/gateway cells vs lakectl-local cells (each note says which face earns what). Everest mount (NFS/FUSE) is enterprise and absent from this repo.

notes.Consistency: lakeFS replaced the filesystem with a KV-CAS commit store: acked writes are already in S3 + KV before the app sees success ({{cmpL:Consistency/Ack survives}}, graveler staging), API readers see staged writes immediately, and branch/merge machinery arbitrates with per-key conflict refusal (graveler.go:2289). The filesystem axes invert — no locks, no rename anywhere in the API, no shared sqlite/git — and foreign S3 writes are the mirror of Lean’s inbox: hidden, served corrupt under a stale ETag, or GC-deleted ({{cmp:Consistency/Conflicts}}). CAS raised 3.5→4 by the critic: refusal-grade KV insert-if-absent outweighs the missing object-level If-Match.
notes.Performance: An envelope of two postures no single workload gets at once: hot-loop 5 and cold start belong to lakectl-local checkouts (plain files, nothing on the I/O path), while metadata-heavy work pays 2–3 HTTPS round-trips per file ({{cmpL:Performance/Small files}}). Streaming rides presigned-direct to S3; scale-out is stateless replicas until the KV store binds (4). Envelope 2.5: every POSIX workload needs a full local copy the repo’s own CLI warns is non-scalable.
notes.Security: The score rests on SigV4 per-request signing at the gateway plus presigned URLs keeping bucket credentials server-side — OIDC/SAML/RBAC are enterprise (pkg/auth/build.go Fatals non-basic modes), so shipped OSS is effectively one superAdmin: tenancy 1.5 is where the split bites. Misconfig lowered 3→2.5 by the verifier: blockstore.signing.secret_key defaults to a publicly-known constant in ALL modes (config/defaults.go:107). Default-on hooks put writer-authored webhooks on the server’s network position.
notes.Day-2 operations: Cheapest fleet citizen per share: a parked repo is KV rows plus bytes (idle 4.5), consumers need only a CLI/SDK (4.5), rolls are stateless restarts. Failure shape lowered 4→3 on review: server/KV death stops the whole data plane for every API/gateway consumer fleet-wide — only lakectl-local working files ride it out — where Lean’s running pods keep serving. And the axes don’t price the structural contrast: Lean operates ZERO databases (the bucket is the DR story); lakeFS carries an operated KV (refs + all uncommitted staging) plus an external Spark GC job. Observability 2.5: no per-repo metrics dimension; /_health checks neither KV nor blockstore.

headlines: lakeFS beats Lean exactly where the server owns the truth — an acked write is already in S3 plus the KV store before the app sees success ({{cmp:Consistency/Ack survives}}), API readers see each other’s staged writes immediately ({{cmp:Consistency/Freshness}}), and branch/merge machinery genuinely arbitrates concurrent writers with per-key conflict refusal ({{cmp:Consistency/Arbitration}}). The structural reason: it replaced the filesystem with a commit store.

Everything filesystem-shaped inverts. No locks, no rename, no shared sqlite/git across clients (1.5); metadata storms pay HTTPS round-trips against Lean’s local-NVMe {{lean:Performance/Small files}}; every POSIX workload needs a full local checkout. The mount that would fix this — Everest, NFS/FUSE write mode — is enterprise and not in this codebase.

On out-of-band writes the two systems mirror each other at the door each one offers: a foreign write through Lean’s gateway is preserved and surfaced by the inbox ({{lean:Consistency/Conflicts}}); lakeFS offers no such door, and a write into its namespace is hidden, scheduled for GC deletion, or served corrupt under an unverified stored ETag ({{lake:Consistency/Conflicts}}). The comparison is narrower than the scores: a write placed straight into Lean’s bucket, bypassing its gateway, is undetected too — its own Conflicts cell says so — and the difference there is the bytes’ fate, not detection. The object store is lakeFS’s private heap, not a shared surface.

As a fleet citizen lakeFS is cheaper than Lean per share — parking is free, consumers featherweight, rolls stateless — but it concentrates what Lean distributes: server/KV death stops the whole API data plane fleet-wide (failure shape {{cmp:Day-2 operations/Failure shape}}), OSS multi-tenancy is one superAdmin (tenancy {{cmp:Security/Tenancy}}), and the default-on hooks engine puts writer-authored synchronous webhooks inside the commit path (pkg/actions, 6.4k LOC — flagged by the critic from a subsystem no scorer had read).
foot: Method: recon → score → adversarial verify (file:line evidence, 452 tool calls) → cross-dimension critique; reconciliation adopted the verifier’s misconfig adjustment and the critic’s CAS raise, upgrades trim, and two-postures caveat. Evidence basis differs from pages 1–3: the flint columns are doc-grounded and drill-proven; this column is code-inferred from one commit (4bb11638) of the OSS repo — Everest mount, RBAC, and OIDC/SAML are enterprise deltas noted per cell. Radar overlays show Lean vs lakeFS; the tables carry every column. Cross-references to Lean cells on this page were re-synced to the live scores on 2026-08-27 — three had been quoting pre-rescore values, which is the hazard of hand-writing one page against another page’s numbers. Post-publication review lowered Day-2 failure shape 4→3: the two-postures envelope had credited the API/gateway face with lakectl-local’s outage behavior.
